stories.headline: Nscale Buys Anyscale for $1.65 Billion in a Bid to Own the Full AI Compute Stack
stories.key_takeaway: British neocloud Nscale is acquiring Ray-maker Anyscale for a reported $1.65 billion to fuse AI orchestration software onto its power-to-GPU stack and capture more of customers' AI spending.

pull_quote.text: Most infrastructure providers just buy GPUs and rent them. Nscale is doing something unique. We build and own every layer ourselves: the power, the data centers, the compute, and the software that turns them into an AI cloud.

stories.article_excerpt: British AI cloud upstart Nscale said on July 30 that it has agreed to acquire Anyscale, the San Francisco software company behind the open-source Ray framework.

stories.headline: Meta's Revenue Jumps 28% to $60.8 Billion as AI Capex Climbs Toward $145 Billion
stories.key_takeaway: Meta's ad business surged 28% to $60.8B in Q2 2026, but a $31.1B quarterly AI capex bill crushed free cash flow to $784M and pushed EPS below estimates, sending the stock down about 10%.

pull_quote.text: I get that this is a big investment and it's a big bet. My personal bet is that the people who invest in this are going to be rewarded and feel very good over time.

stories.article_excerpt: Meta's advertising machine is still running hot. The number investors fixated on was smaller: free cash flow of just $784 million, gutted by an AI buildout.

stories.headline: Freehand Raises $75 Million Series B to Automate Enterprise Supply Chains With AI
stories.key_takeaway: Freehand raised a $75M Series B co-led by Battery Ventures and NewRoad Capital Partners, bringing its total to ~$100M, to scale autonomous AI agents that run supply-chain spend for Fortune 500 firms.

pull_quote.text: Enterprises spend $16 billion a year on supply chain software and another $348 billion hiring people to do what this software cannot. We built Freehand to close that gap.

stories.article_excerpt: San Francisco startup Freehand said on July 29 that it has raised $75 million to expand a fleet of autonomous AI agents that already run supply-chain spending for some of the world's largest companies.

stories.headline: Encore AI Lands $30 Million to Turn Top Salespeople's Habits Into AI Agents
stories.key_takeaway: Encore AI (formerly Insait IO) raised a $30M Series A led by Team8, Planven and The Garage to scale 'interaction mining' tech that distills top performers' behaviors from calls, emails and CRM data and deploys them as revenue-generating AI agents.

pull_quote.text: Sometimes our agents even tell the jokes that the relationship managers are telling, because we literally run by the playbooks that we see working.

stories.article_excerpt: Every sales floor has them: the handful of reps who close deals nobody else can. Encore AI has raised $30 million to bottle that instinct and hand it to a machine.

stories.headline: Microsoft and Mistral Expand Their Alliance to Sell Controllable Frontier AI to Regulated Industries
stories.key_takeaway: Microsoft is committing billions to Mistral's European GPU fleet and embedding Mistral's models across Foundry and Copilot Studio, pitching controllable, sovereign frontier AI to regulated industries while hedging its dependence on OpenAI.

pull_quote.text: Europe should have access to the world's most capable AI without compromising control over their data, operations or digital future.

data_points.label: MS commitment to Mistral EU compute

stories.article_excerpt: Microsoft and Mistral have deepened a two-year-old alliance into a multibillion-dollar bet that the next wave of enterprise AI will be won on where and how that power can be controlled.

stories.headline: Google Turns Gemini Into an App Builder, Generating Interactive Software From a Prompt
stories.key_takeaway: Google is extending Gemini from text generation to software generation, with a new 'App' artifact in Gemini Notebook and a shipping Canvas mode that builds interactive apps from a prompt, pushing into the prompt-to-app race against OpenAI Canvas and Claude Artifacts.

pull_quote.text: The question used to be: what information should this page contain? The question now is: what can visitors do with this page?
pull_quote.role: AI consultant, on Gemini Canvas app generation

data_points.label: Canvas rolled out in Search AI Mode
Languages for Fill with Gemini in Sheets

stories.article_excerpt: Google is quietly reshaping Gemini from a chatbot that writes text into a tool that writes working software, with a new 'App' artifact that turns documents into an interactive application.

stories.headline: Ant Group Open-Sources LingBot-VLA 2.0, a Vision-Language-Action Model for Robots
stories.key_takeaway: Ant Group's Robbyant unit open-sourced LingBot-VLA 2.0, a ~6B-parameter vision-language-action model under Apache 2.0 that controls 20-plus robot configurations from 17 manufacturers through a shared action space, putting China at the center of the open embodied-AI race.
stories.article_excerpt: Ant Group's robotics arm has thrown a fully open, general-purpose 'robot brain' into the race to build software that can run almost any machine.

stories.headline: GitHub Ends Unlimited Copilot, Shifting Developers to Metered 'AI Credits'
stories.key_takeaway: GitHub replaced Copilot's flat premium-request subscription with token-metered 'AI Credits' (1 credit = $0.01), keeping base plan prices flat but sparking backlash as developers burn through monthly allotments in hours.

pull_quote.text: GitHub has absorbed much of the escalating inference cost behind that usage, but the current premium request model is no longer sustainable.

stories.article_excerpt: The era of the all-you-can-code Copilot subscription is over. GitHub retired the flat 'premium request' model and replaced it with metered billing denominated in AI Credits.

stories.headline: Cognizant Deepens Its Anthropic Alliance to Push Claude Across Enterprise Clients
stories.key_takeaway: Cognizant became a top-tier Global Premier Partner in Anthropic's Claude Partner Network on July 27, 2026, embedding Claude across its platforms and training 30,000+ associates, turning its huge workforce into a Claude distribution channel for regulated industries.

pull_quote.text: AI capability is rising faster than enterprises can absorb it, and that gap is the defining problem of this moment. Our role is to be the bridge.

stories.article_excerpt: One of the world's largest IT services firms just made itself a preferred distribution channel for Anthropic's Claude, installed as a Global Premier Partner.

stories.headline: New Research Lets Teams of AI Agents Rewire Who Talks to Whom, Round by Round
stories.key_takeaway: DyTopo replaces fixed multi-agent communication structures with a graph that is rebuilt each reasoning round via semantic matching, reporting an average +6.2 gain over the strongest baseline across code and math benchmarks on four LLM backbones.

pull_quote.text: DyTopo, a manager-guided multi-agent framework that reconstructs a sparse directed communication graph at each round.

stories.article_excerpt: When engineers wire several LLMs into a team, they almost always fix the plumbing in advance. DyTopo argues the map of who-talks-to-whom should be redrawn every round.

stories.headline: Can AI Agents Do Open-Ended Science? New Case Studies Offer Early Evidence
stories.key_takeaway: A Princeton-led team tested frontier AI agents on the real, unpublished research questions behind two NeurIPS 2026 submissions, grading them via the papers' original authors; the agents handled all the engineering but failed to make substantial research progress.

pull_quote.text: The agents completed all of the engineering without human help, yet could not make substantial progress towards answering the research questions.

stories.article_excerpt: A paper posted to arXiv on July 29 puts the bet that AI can automate its own research to an unusually honest test, and the early answer is a qualified no.

stories.headline: Robots Learn to 'Think Longer' at Test Time With Latent Reasoning Loops
stories.key_takeaway: RD-VLA lets robot vision-language-action models iterate silently in latent space at inference, scaling test-time compute with constant memory and turning some 0%-success tasks into 90%+ success with four reasoning loops.

pull_quote.text: Tasks that fail entirely with single-iteration inference exceed 90 percent success with four iterations, while simpler tasks saturate rapidly.

stories.article_excerpt: Robotics researchers want to bring inference-time reasoning to machines that move in the physical world, without the latency that made chatbot-style chain-of-thought a poor fit.

stories.headline: AI Systems Are Cracking Olympiad Math by Generating and Testing Their Own Proof Strategies
stories.key_takeaway: AI systems have moved from silver (IMO 2024) to gold-medal standard (IMO 2025) by treating proofs as search problems, generating candidate strategies, scoring their plausibility and systematically exploring the strongest, an approach now applied to open research problems.
stories.article_excerpt: For decades, the International Mathematical Olympiad was a stress test that machines flunked. That barrier has now fallen twice over.

stories.headline: EU Opens Bidding for Seven AI 'Gigafactories,' Pledging Euro 10 Billion to Close the Compute Gap
stories.key_takeaway: The EU opened bidding for seven AI gigafactories, pledging up to 10 billion euros in public funds to unlock over 30 billion euros total, each site to hold 100,000+ AI chips, in a bid to close the compute gap with the US and China.

pull_quote.text: Access to the raw scale of computing power within AI Gigafactories is a strategic necessity for Europe as AI development accelerates.

stories.article_excerpt: The EU threw down its biggest bet yet on catching the US and China in AI, opening a formal call for tenders to build seven AI 'gigafactories' across the bloc.

stories.headline: China's First Binding Rules for AI Agents Take Hold, Setting a Global Template
stories.key_takeaway: China's Implementation Opinions on Intelligent Agents and the binding Interim Measures on Anthropomorphic AI Interaction Services both took effect July 15, 2026, making China the first jurisdiction to regulate AI agents as a distinct category via a three-tier decision-authorization framework.

pull_quote.text: The Opinions signal that China is beginning to regulate AI agents as a distinct governance category rather than simply treating them as an extension of generative AI.

stories.article_excerpt: On July 15, 2026, China became the first country to carve out a dedicated regulatory category for AI agents, jointly issued by the CAC, NDRC and MIIT.

stories.headline: China's New AI Companion Rules Take Effect, Forcing Chatbots to Prove You're Not a Kid
stories.key_takeaway: China's Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interactive Services took effect July 15, 2026, forcing companion chatbots to verify users' ages, ban virtual intimacy for minors and add anti-addiction safeguards, prompting ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen to shut features down.

pull_quote.text: Current agents are not yet mature.

stories.article_excerpt: Hundreds of millions of Chinese users who built AI companions woke up on July 15 to find the machines switched off, the day China's first companion-AI rulebook took effect.
